title: Yuzu Curd Tart with Raspberries
changes_from_base: A silky blended yuzu curd in a press-in lemon crust with a ring of raspberries, instead of crème pâtissière under mixed fruit.
summary: A press-in lemon crust filled with a silky blended yuzu curd and edged with fresh raspberries.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cubed, plus extra for the tin
bottled pure yuzu juice, or Meyer lemon juice

steps.title: Crumb dough
steps.text: heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Pulse the flour, icing sugar, lemon zest and salt, add the butter and pulse until sandy, then pulse in the yolk.

steps.title: Squeeze a little
steps.text: if it doesn't hold, add 1-2 tbsp cold water.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: butter the tin and press the dough evenly over the base and up the sides, saving a little for repairs.

steps.title: Bake the case
steps.text: line with foil tucked over the edges and bake on the tray 20-25 min, until dry. Remove the foil, patch any cracks and bake 5-10 min more, until golden. Cool completely.

steps.title: Curd
steps.text: set the sieve over the bowl. Whisk the yuzu juice, sugar, eggs and yolks smooth in the pan, then whisk over medium-low heat until thick and 80 °C on the thermometer. Sieve at once. Whisk constantly so the eggs cook evenly.

steps.title: Cool slightly
steps.text: chill 10-15 min, stirring now and then, until just warm.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: pour into the blender and, on medium speed, drop in the butter piece by piece until creamy. If it is very bubbly, let it sit 5 min. Blending in the butter gives a light, creamy curd.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: pour into the case and chill about 2 h. Scatter the raspberries round the edge just before serving.

tips: Bottled yuzu juice is sold in Japanese and Asian shops; check it is 100% juice.
Meyer lemons are a good stand-in if you cannot find yuzu.
Add the raspberries at the last minute so they don't bleed into the curd.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
